learning_outcomes.text: Students are able to recognize and name the anthropogenic environmental crises threatening our planet in their complexity.
Students are able to evaluate the sustainability strategies of efficiency, sufficiency, and consistency and implement them as possible approaches in course-specific solution methods.
They understand evaluation instruments such as life cycle assessments and know various evaluation concepts (CO2 balance, MIPS, LCSA, etc.).

Students develop sensitivity for resource consumption, CO2 generation, and the avoidance of all environmental damage in material selection, design, and production, i.e., for the development of climate-neutral and sustainable products.
Students are enabled to comprehend the complexity of the interaction between human action and the global environment with regard to environmental destruction and sustainable development.
They are able to classify and assess the importance of sustainability issues in engineering and business contexts.
They acquire methodological competencies for planning and concrete implementation of sustainability measures and can organizationally support and document practical implementation.

syllabus_topics: Description of the UN Sustainable (Social) Development Goals (SDG)
Description and evaluation of anthropogenic environmental crises in their entirety - including political, economic, and social consequences
Discussion of sustainability strategies: efficiency, sufficiency, and consistency
Three-pillar model of sustainability (ecology, economy, social)
Legislation and standards (quality marks, key figures and criteria)
Identification of psychological and political obstacles in overcoming a sustainable transformation of society
Sustainability at one's own university (mission statement, working groups, etc.)
Analysis options for fake news, old ways of thinking, and greenwashing
Evaluation methodology (life cycle assessment, MIPS, LCSA, etc.)
assessment_rules: To receive credit points, the module exam must be passed. The weighting for the final grade is based on credit points.
